text:
maya: FYI customer on Dedicated cluster `eu-west-2-ded-14` opened a support case — spikes of 500s and tail latency for text-generation around 2025-11-18 14:22 UTC. They included request id `req_0x9a1b2c`. Can infra/sre help collect logs + GPU metrics for repro?

james: On it. Do we have a curl repro from the customer or a sample request body? Also need the exact pod names if they already saw an error in logs.

maya: They sent a quick curl. Pasting below (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-request-id: req_0x9a1b2c" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3a", "input":"Summarize the following...", "max_tokens":1024}'
```

maya: They say it fails ~1 in 8 requests with a 500 body: `{"error":"worker_error","code":500}` and the latency for successful ones jumps to 2–3s. Reported for ~3 hours.

tess: Thanks — I'll start with pod-level logs for the dedicated pool. Steps I'm going to run:
1) list serving pods for that dedicated pool
```bash
kubectl -n redwood-serving get pods -l dedicated-pool=eu-west-2-ded-14 -o name
```
2) tail logs for the pod that handled the request (if we can find it):
```bash
kubectl -n redwood-serving logs <pod-name> -c runtime --since=2h | grep req_0x9a1b2c -A5 -B2
```
3) describe pod and check events:
```bash
kubectl -n redwood-serving describe pod <pod-name>
```
4) check node syslogs and container runtime errors:
```bash
ssh node-XXX
sudo journalctl -u containerd --no-pager --since "2025-11-18 12:00" | tail -n 200
```
5) GPU metrics:
```bash
ssh node-XXX
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu --format=csv -i 0
# and from prometheus: curl -s "http://prometheus.service/api/v1/query?query=avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_utilization[5m])"
```
I'll collect pod logs + node journal + nvidia-smi snapshot + `kubectl get events`.

chris: Quick note: also check runtime logs for KV cache hits/misses and any OOM kills. If there's a model compilation fallback, those show up in the runtime logs right before latency spikes. Grep for `kv_cache` and `compilation` in the same timespan.

maya: I asked the customer for their full request-ids list — they gave `req_0x9a1b2c`, `req_0x9a1b2d`, `req_0x9a1b2f`. All in the same hour window. I told them we'll collect a debug bundle and provided a support upload.

james: To standardize the bundle we use our support helper. Running on a jumphost: 
```bash
sudo /opt/redwood/bin/collect-debug-bundle.sh 
  --cluster eu-west-2-ded-14 
  --requests req_0x9a1b2c,req_0x9a1b2d,req_0x9a1b2f 
  --since "2025-11-18T13:30:00Z" 
  --until "2025-11-18T15:30:00Z" 
  --output /tmp/redwood-debug-eu-west-2-ded-14-1759123456.tar.gz
```
That script collects: pod logs, node journal, container runtime metadata, prometheus snapshots for GPU metrics, `kubectl describe` outputs, and runtime traces. It runs as root and may take ~2–3 minutes.

support-bot: deploy-bot noticed a canary rollout at 2025-11-18T14:13:00Z to pool `eu-west-2-ded-14` (deploy id: dply-3291). Might be related.

chris: Good catch. If there was a canary we should correlate deploy timestamps with the first error. Also check model binary version and quantization flags in the runtime logs.

james: After the bundle is created, upload to our private S3 bucket with the support ticket number. I'll create the storage presigned URL and post it here. Also adding steps if we need deeper traces: enable verbose runtime tracing for 10 minutes for the affected pool: 
```bash
kubectl -n redwood-serving set env deployment/runtime --env RUNTIME_LOG_LEVEL=debug --record
# revert after repro window
```

maya: I'll ask the customer to run the sanitized curl against a canary endpoint we control so we can get live request logs: `https://canary-east.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — I've given them a temp token and asked them to include `x-request-id` header.

tess: I've started collecting logs now — grabbing pod list + `kubectl logs` for the three request ids and a `nvidia-smi` snapshot from each node. If I find container restarts or OOMKilled events I'll post them here.

james: If anyone needs to look at node-level GPU telemetry beyond snapshots, query prometheus for `nvidia_gpu_memory_total_bytes` and `nvidia_gpu_memory_used_bytes` for the node for that hour. Example: 
```bash
# prom api example
curl -s "http://prometheus.service/api/v1/query_range?query=nvidia_gpu_memory_used_bytes%7Bnode=~\"node-.*\"%7D&start=1700300000&end=1700307200&step=60" | jq .
```

maya: Thanks all — I'll post the upload link + ticket id once the bundle is ready. Customer asked for ETA; told them ~1–2 business hours for initial findings.

support-bot: debug bundle uploaded: s3://support-debug-uploads/redwood-debug-eu-west-2-ded-14-1759123456.tar.gz (internal access). Ticket #SUP-3429.

chris: I'll pull the bundle and run the repro locally against a patched canary to see if I can force the 500 and capture runtime stack traces.

james: Good. If we repro, next steps: 1) capture runtime stack + heap, 2) get GPU process list (ps -ef | grep model_server) at the time, 3) check kernel dmesg for any GPU driver errors.

maya: I'll update the customer with ticket #SUP-3429 and that SRE/infra are investigating.

(ends)
